title: Transit & Escape Tactics
description: Advanced situational awareness for public transport and recognizing when an environment is becoming unsafe.

scenes.text: You are taking the bus home late in the evening. The bus is mostly empty. A man boards the bus and, despite many empty seats, sits right next to you. He starts asking you personal questions about where you live.
How should you respond to this invasion of space?

choices.text: Answer his questions to be polite, but look away.
choices.feedbackText: You do not owe strangers politeness if they make you uncomfortable. Giving out personal information is dangerous.

choices.text: Stand up, say nothing, and move to a seat near the bus conductor or driver.
choices.feedbackText: Excellent! You removed yourself from the uncomfortable situation and moved to a 'safe zone' near authority figures (the driver).

scenes.text: You stand up to move. Tap on the safest place to sit on this bus.

choices.feedbackText: Yes! Sitting near the driver or conductor means you are visible and they can assist you if needed.
The safest place is at the front of the bus, near the driver or conductor.

scenes.text: You sit near the driver. The man gets off at the next stop. You successfully used situational awareness and preventative action to stay safe!
